title: On phase-isometries between the unit spheres of the Banach space of continuous real-valued functions
summary: For a locally compact Hausdorff space $L$, we denote by $C_0(L,\mathbb{R})$ the Banach space of all continuous real-valued functions on $L$ vanishing at infinity, endowed with the supremum norm. In this paper, we prove that every surjective phase-isometry $T\colon S(C_0(X,\mathbb{R}))\to S(C_0(Y,\mathbb{R}))$ between the unit spheres of $C_0(X,\mathbb{R})$ and $C_0(Y,\mathbb{R})$ is a variant of a weighted composition operator in the following sense: there exist a function $\varepsilon\colon S(C_0(X,\mathbb{R}))\to\{-1,1\}$,a continuous function $α\colon Y\to \{-1,1\}$ and a homeomorphism…
